study type: Secondary data analysis of a 24-week, two-arm exercise intervention trial
cohort: 125 pregnant women (58 exercisers and 67 controls) with singleton pregnancies, aged 18-40 years, BMI between 18.5-34.99 kg/m(2), and no preexisting health conditions
finding: Prenatal exercise may attenuate the racial/ethnic disparities observed in neonatal birth weight, and possibly gestational age and preterm birth in Non-Hispanic Black pregnant women compared to Non-Hispanic White pregnant women.
mod_finding: Prenatal exercise did not have significant effects on the risk of cesarean section.
birth_weight: Low birth weight defined as < 2.5 kg
